name: Kaunas University of Technology
summary: Technical university in Kaunas; 26 English-taught bachelor's and integrated degrees in engineering, informatics, sciences and business.

ib.text: KTU scores your IB grades: maths or a programme subject, a second subject and English, each above 60%. English needs B2 (IELTS 5.5 or equivalent). Finishing the IB adds 0.5 bonus points.

programmes.name: Applied Chemistry
programmes.about: Chemistry for new products from cosmetics to pharmaceuticals and functional materials, with laboratory practice in synthesising and testing new materials.
programmes.overview: The early semesters cover mathematics, physics, inorganic and organic chemistry, cell biology and physical chemistry, followed by chemical analysis, polymer and colloid chemistry, biochemistry, instrumental analysis, functional materials and process engineering. Later options reach into cosmetics chemistry, drug chemistry and technology, toxicology and sustainable chemistry. Laboratory work is constant, and you can join research groups from the first year, complete a product development project and two internships. Two pathways are offered, Innovation Development with industry partners or Pedagogy for a teaching qualification. Graduates work as chemists and quality control specialists in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, materials and energy.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is chemistry 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: Biomedical Materials Industries
programmes.credential: Bachelor of Technological and Physical Sciences
programmes.about: Chemistry, biology and engineering combined to develop materials and medical devices for medicine.
programmes.overview: The course draws on chemistry, biology and engineering: organic, physical and polymer chemistry sit beside cell and molecular biology, human anatomy, tissue engineering, biomedical materials science and process engineering. Instrumental analysis, toxicology and risk assessment and good manufacturing practice prepare you for industry. You work in specialised laboratories, complete a product development project, two internships and a final project. Pathways in Innovation Development or Pedagogy are available, and exchange partners include Aveiro and the Technical University of Denmark. Graduates develop biomedical materials and technologies or work as experts and researchers in companies such as Thermo Fisher Scientific.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Chemical Technology and Engineering
programmes.about: Chemical engineering beyond theory: creating new materials, controlling processes and solving industrial problems.
programmes.overview: The first years build mathematics, physics, inorganic, organic and physical chemistry, chemical analysis, engineering graphics and general chemical technology, then move on to instrumental analysis, materials science, process engineering, process modelling and chemical thermodynamics. The final year brings chemical engineering design, a project practicum, a professional internship and the bachelor thesis. You work in process research and control laboratories and choose between Organic Materials (plastics, elastomers, refining, paper and textiles) and Inorganic Materials (acids, fertilizers, ceramics, glass). A double degree with the University of Carthage is possible. Graduates work as technologists and project engineers, including in hydrogen and renewable energy.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Food Science and Technology
programmes.about: Food chemistry, microbiology, nutrition and technology for food safety, quality and sustainability.
programmes.overview: Chemistry (inorganic, organic, physical), biology, mathematics and physics lead into food chemistry and analysis, food microbiology and hygiene, food technologies, sensory evaluation, nutrition and metabolism, and food quality and safety. Electives include sustainable food systems, toxicology and molecular gastronomy. You work in laboratories with analytical and pilot-scale equipment, on product development projects and real technological cases with industry practitioners, and complete two internships. Learning routes are challenge-based learning, Innovation Development or Pedagogy. Exchange partners include Wageningen and the Technical University of Denmark. Graduates become food technologists, quality controllers, nutritionists or product developers.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Industrial Biotechnology
programmes.about: Biotechnological processes, molecular biology, genetic engineering, bioinformatics and bioprocess engineering to make bioproducts for industry.
programmes.overview: Over eight semesters mathematics, physics, chemistry, cell biology and microbiology lead into molecular biology, genetic engineering, bioinformatics, instrumental analysis and bioprocess engineering, then enzymology, polymer chemistry, biotechnology equipment design and process optimisation. You experiment hands-on with micro-organisms, yeast, plant and algal cells in laboratories, take on a product development project, and finish with a professional internship and a bachelor thesis project. An Innovation Development or Pedagogy pathway is optional, and Erasmus+ exchanges include Wageningen and Padova. Graduates work as bioproduct production technologists, quality assurance specialists and innovation coordinators.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Architecture
programmes.about: Integrated five-year degree in designing buildings and urban space, with practical projects alongside civil engineering students; qualifies you to practise as an architect across the EU.
programmes.overview: This integrated five-year programme runs studio-based design from fundamentals through residential and public buildings and building complexes to landscape design, alongside building physics, structures, BIM, energy performance, construction planning, architectural history and theory, heritage and urban planning. You work in close contact with lecturers and on joint projects with civil engineering students. A long professional internship in the sixth semester, research projects and a master thesis complete the degree. You choose between building design, landscape architecture and urban planning. Graduates become architects, urbanists or landscape architects, and the diploma allows practice across the EU.
programmes.selectionNote: A digital portfolio of up to 8 projects, then a remote artistic entrance exam (three sittings in 2026) for selected applicants; 2026 procedure, 2027 not yet published.
programmes.ib: Judged on a portfolio, a remote drawing entrance exam and maybe an interview; maths, IT or physics and English from your IB grades also count.

programmes.name: Automation and Control
programmes.about: Designing automation from machine control to intelligent systems, robotics and AI.
programmes.overview: Eight semesters build from physics, mathematics, programming and circuit analysis to automatic control theory, electric drives, instrumentation and logical automation, with modules on artificial intelligence, computer vision and digital twins. From the fifth semester you specialise in Control Systems, Mechatronic Systems or Process Control. Practical work uses laboratories and real industrial equipment, and the last semester combines a professional internship with the final project. Exchange partners include Aalto, Lund and Hiroshima. Graduates work as control systems engineers and designers and automation systems programmers.

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Electrical machines, power electronics and energy converters, with design and operation of power and energy systems.
programmes.overview: After physics, mathematics, programming and engineering materials, you study electric circuits, electromechanics, applied and power electronics, high voltage engineering, automatic control, electric drives, electrical networks and power system elements. You specialise in either Energy Converters and Control or Information Technology of Electrical Engineering, and can add an Innovation Development path or a Pedagogy minor. Laboratories include distributed generation and power plant facilities, a product development project comes in semester six, and an internship and thesis project end the degree. Exchange partners include DTU, Lund and Linkoping. Graduates work in power generation, distribution and smart grids.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

separateFrom.name: Electronics and Electrical Engineering
separateFrom.reason: Different programme: a 3-year English-only degree combining electronics and electrical engineering; this one is 4 years and focused on power and energy systems.

programmes.name: Electronics and Electrical Engineering
programmes.about: Electronics and electrical engineering in one three-year programme, for developing advanced and safe electronic and electrical systems; English only.
programmes.overview: Six semesters cover mathematics, physics, circuit theory, signal processing, analogue, digital and power electronics, microprocessor systems with embedded programming, power systems and smart grids, and measurement. Teaching happens in numerous teaching laboratories and FabLab Kaunas, with guest lectures from industry. A product development project comes in semester four, and a professional internship and final project close the degree. Exchange partners include Korea University and Vienna University of Technology. The mix of electronics and power leads to roles as electronics or electrical engineers or smart systems architects, and on to postgraduate study in either field.

programmes.name: Renewable Energy Engineering
programmes.about: Solar, wind, hydro and biofuel technologies and how to apply them in energy production and use, with hands-on laboratory training.
programmes.overview: Physics, mathematics, programming, thermodynamics and circuit analysis lead to electrical machines for renewable sources, power engineering, heat transfer and control theory, with topics on solar, wind, hydro, geothermal, heat pumps, biomass, fuel cells, energy storage and nuclear fundamentals. You train in laboratories with Siemens and ABB equipment and in the storage and smart grid centres, with mandatory placements at energy companies, visits to power facilities and a final project. Two tracks are offered, Smart Electric Power Systems or Sustainable Thermal Energy Systems. Graduates work as renewable energy integration specialists, thermal energy engineers or digital transformation specialists.

programmes.name: Robotics
programmes.about: Designing, programming and training robots for homes, space or industry, with computer science, electronics and control.
programmes.overview: Eight semesters combine physics, mathematics, programming and circuit analysis with control technologies, electromechanics, robot kinematics and dynamics, microprocessors, image processing, intelligent control, robot programming and simulation, plus AI ethics. You learn in robotics laboratories and the Rockwell Automation Training Centre, build object models and run simulations with robot digital twins, and hear from companies such as ABB, Omron and Elinta Robotics. A professional internship and a bachelor thesis project finish the course. Innovation Development and Pedagogy pathways are open, with exchanges to Hiroshima and DTU. Graduates work as robotics engineers, system designers and robot programmers.

programmes.name: Transport Electronics
programmes.about: Electronics for electric and autonomous vehicles and intelligent transport: design, diagnostics and engine management technologies. Also offered part-time over six years.
programmes.overview: You study mathematics, physics, electronics, circuit theory, programming in Matlab, Python and C++, signals and systems, microprocessors and automotive electronic systems, with emphasis on transport sensors and testing and diagnostic systems. Further topics include embedded design, autonomous vehicle control, traffic flow control and AI in electronic systems. Teams design and build working prototypes in semester projects, and the university has an advanced automotive diagnostics laboratory. The last semester combines a professional internship with the bachelor final project. Graduates work as transport electronics, diagnostic and maintenance engineers or design engineers for autonomous transport systems.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Artificial Intelligence
programmes.about: Building intelligent software with machine learning, image recognition and data analysis, applied to business, academic and public-sector problems.
programmes.overview: You start with object-oriented programming, mathematics, digital logic, databases, data structures and discrete structures, then study machine learning, deep learning, image processing, speech recognition, cloud computing for AI, multi-agent systems, computer architecture, operating systems and software engineering. Lectures from active researchers are mixed with practitioner guest talks, a team-based product development project comes in semester six, and an internship in semester eight finishes the degree. Innovation Development lets you build products with partners, and exchange partners include Deusto and Bologna. Graduates work as AI solutions developers, AI systems analysts and developers of human-assisted intelligent systems.
programmes.selectionNote: Half the score is a maths entry exam, 30% a second subject and 20% English; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: Informatics
programmes.about: Programming, 3D models, cloud and mobile networks, web solutions and multimedia, with internet informatics and multimedia systems paths.
programmes.overview: Eight semesters cover object-oriented programming, mathematics, digital logic, data structures, computer architecture, databases, operating systems, algorithms, software engineering, networks and concurrent programming. From the fifth semester you specialise in Internet Informatics (web applications, cloud, network security) or Multimedia Systems (visual design, 3D modelling, digital audio and video, virtual reality), with optional depth in machine learning, cryptography or data analytics. A product development project with partners in semester six, access to high-performance computing, and a final internship and project make up the practice. Graduates work as software developers, systems analysts or digital twinning engineers.
programmes.selectionNote: Half the score is a maths entry exam, 30% a second subject and 20% English; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: Engineering Physics
programmes.about: Physics with AI and measurement solutions: micro- and nanoelectronics, nanotechnology, advanced materials, IoT and photonics.
programmes.overview: The core is chemistry, mathematics, classical mechanics, electromagnetism, thermodynamics and statistical physics, quantum mechanics and solid state physics, applied through Python programming, computer-aided design, electronics, machine learning, optics and light technologies and metrology. Electives can lead toward nuclear and particle physics or computational intelligence. You work in modern laboratories, complete a product development project in semester six, then an engineering internship and a final project. Innovation Development and Pedagogy pathways are open, and exchanges include DTU and Aveiro. Graduates work as engineering technologists, renewable energy technologists or quantum systems metrologists.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is physics 40%, a second subject 20% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: Materials Physics and Nanotechnologies
programmes.credential: Bachelor of Technological and Physical Sciences
programmes.about: Advanced materials, semiconductors and nanotechnology in a programme joining materials physics and nanotechnology.
programmes.overview: Over four years you study chemistry, mathematics, classical and quantum mechanics, thermodynamics, electrodynamics, solid state physics, nuclear and particle physics and the physics of materials, then micro- and nanotechnology, thin films, functional materials and nanophotonics. Teaching is built around smart laboratories where students research alongside lecturers, a product development project and a final bachelor project, plus a professional internship. Routes include challenge-based learning, Innovation Development and Pedagogy, with Erasmus+ exchanges in Denmark, Portugal, China and South Korea. Graduates work as materials engineers, quantum computer technicians or nanorobot engineers, or continue to master's and doctoral research.

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Aviation Engineering
programmes.about: Aerodynamics, aircraft design and control of unmanned aerial vehicles, with aircraft systems design and maintenance specialisations.
programmes.overview: Mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering drawing and CAD lead into aerodynamics, aircraft types and systems, unmanned aerial vehicles, aviation materials, avionics and aviation engines, with thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, structural integrity, human factors and air law alongside. Learning is problem- and project-based, with student projects such as a flying aerodynamics laboratory and a human-powered aircraft, laboratory work with licensed aviation professionals, and a final-year internship. You choose between Aircraft Design and Aircraft Technical Maintenance. Exchanges include IPSA in France and Limerick. Graduates work as aircraft designers, aeronautical technologists or hybrid electric aircraft developers in design, repair and aerospace companies.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Fashion Engineering
programmes.about: Digital design technologies, advanced textiles and sustainable, functional clothing for people interested in fashion and technology.
programmes.overview: You combine mathematics, physics, chemistry and materials science with textile technologies, clothing pattern construction, fashion design and digital tools such as Lectra, Gerber CAD and Adobe Creative Suite, and later functional textiles, textile recycling, knit design and virtual fashion creation. Teaching includes pattern modelling, prototyping and garment construction in labs, digital design studios, company visits and real-world cases, with exchange semesters at European partners such as Boras and Liberec. A bachelor thesis or professional internship ends the degree, and electives let you lean toward design, marketing, business or virtual fashion. Graduates work as clothing designers, textile experts or virtual fashion specialists.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Industrial Engineering
programmes.about: Optimising production, developing prototypes, robotic solutions and digital manufacturing, plus management skills.
programmes.overview: The programme covers mathematics, physics, engineering mechanics, thermodynamics, electrotechnics, materials science of metals, ceramics and polymers, CAD, quality assurance, ergonomics and manufacturing technologies, then additive manufacturing, Industry 4.0 and robotic systems. Laboratory work combines with product development projects, semester-long capstones and a work placement in Lithuanian or international companies. You choose between Digital Manufacturing and Production and Manufacturing Management, and can follow an extended-internship route. Exchanges include the Technical University of Denmark and Southern Denmark. Graduates work as process improvement specialists, sustainable production project managers or autonomous factory developers.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Mechanical Engineering
programmes.about: Designing manufacturing systems, machines, vehicles and intelligent technologies, with four pathways to choose from.
programmes.overview: You begin with mathematics, physics, chemistry, engineering drawing, thermodynamics, mechanics and materials science, then CAD, machine dynamics, manufacturing engineering and structural integrity. From year two you choose Biomechanics, Mechanical Systems Design, Robotics Engineering or Thermal Systems Engineering. Learning uses laboratories with GUNT systems, CNC machines, Festo robotic kits and 3D prototyping, software such as SolidWorks and Autodesk Inventor, and real engineering problems solved through modelling and optimisation. A mandatory work placement and final project fall in year four, with routes for deeper specialisation, innovation development or extended practice. Graduates work as design engineers, production technologists or biomechanical engineers.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Mechatronics
programmes.about: Mechanics, electronics, IT and programming combined to design and operate robotic and automated systems; taught in English only.
programmes.overview: Mechanics, electronics and programming are taught together across eight semesters, through mathematics, physics, engineering drawing, CAD, thermodynamics, electronics, control systems, robotics and manufacturing technologies. Laboratories include Festo production lines, 3D printers, ABB robots and CNC machine tools, and semester projects have you solve real problems and build working prototypes. Professional internships and a capstone project complete the degree, an Innovation Development pathway lets you build products with partners, and exchanges include Chalmers and Tampere. Graduates work as automated systems engineers, robotics engineers or digital twin developers in manufacturing, aerospace, biomedical and automation sectors.

needs.note: Second subject, 40%: one of these (or engineering technologies)

programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths 40%, a second subject 40% and English 20%, from your IB grades; each entry subject above 60%. Fee-paying; state-funded via LAMA BPO.

programmes.name: Communication Studies and Information Management Technologies
programmes.about: Content creation and technological solutions for communication in global business and public-sector projects.
programmes.overview: Six semesters cover communication theories, organisational and political communication, public relations, risk and crisis communication, audiovisual production, data journalism and information systems design, with research methods, data and text analytics, graphic design, digital marketing and interface design. Academic English at C1 level and creative and media writing sit alongside electives such as media psychology. You work on product development projects and communication campaigns and complete a semester-long internship and a final project. The programme runs as a twin degree with the University of Twente in the Netherlands. Graduates work in communications and marketing, content development and information management.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is English 40%, a second subject 40% and an oral motivation assessment 20%; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: New Media Language
programmes.about: English-language programme for managing projects and writing copy for news portals, websites, social media, advertising and entertainment, with an international teaching team.
programmes.overview: You study linguistics, media culture, discourse analysis and applied linguistics together with writing for different platforms: academic, creative, technical and web content, plus video and audio editing and public speaking. English is taken to C1 level, and you add a second language from French, German, Russian, Spanish or Swedish. Practical work includes creating digital content with Adobe tools and WordPress, challenge-based tasks, a product development project, a professional internship and a bachelor thesis. Exchange routes run through the Applied European Languages network with Spain and France. Graduates work as digital media strategists, content developers, transmedia storytellers, social media managers and digital marketers.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is English 50%, a second subject 30% and an oral motivation assessment 20%; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: Public Policy and Administration
programmes.about: New programme on public policy and administration: analysing societal challenges and making evidence-based decisions at national and international level. Needs ministry approval.
programmes.overview: The curriculum covers political theory, comparative politics, international relations, administrative law and public governance, with modules on Eastern European politics, European Union policy, public finance management, the civil service, and ethics and corruption prevention, plus research methods and digital transformation of the public sector. You work in interdisciplinary teams on a product development project, complete a professional internship and write a final project. Electives let you lean toward Local and Regional Government or Political Communication and Technology. Graduates work as policy analysts, project managers or civil servants, or continue to master's study in political science, public administration, sociology or management.
programmes.ib: New programme, subject to approval by the Ministry of Education, Science and Sport; 2027 criteria not yet published.
programmes.selectionNote: Entry subjects and weights are not published yet. KTU ranks on school grades in the entry subjects, each above 60%. Starts only with ministry approval.

programmes.name: Business Digitalization Management
programmes.about: Bringing AI, robotics, big data, virtual reality and IoT into business processes, for careers as digitalisation managers.
programmes.overview: Eight semesters start with informatics, mathematics and economics, then management, accounting, financial management, marketing and human resources, combined with databases, programming, business intelligence, data mining and process automation. Specialist topics include project, change and innovation management, digital marketing and artificial intelligence in business. Teaching uses challenge-based learning, business simulations and the DigiLab with UiPath software, and an internship of up to a year in Lithuanian or international companies falls in semesters six and seven, followed by a final project. Graduates work as business analysts, digitisation project managers or digital transformation specialists.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths or economics 40%, a second subject 40% and an oral motivation assessment 20%; each entry subject above 60%.

programmes.name: Economics
programmes.about: Economics and analytics: how societies, governments and businesses decide, with data analysis and BA+ competence blocks to choose from.
programmes.overview: Core study covers microeconomics, macroeconomics, econometrics, accounting, finance and data analytics, supported by mathematics, statistics, marketing, business law and the history of economic thought. Case studies, business simulations and professional tools such as Bloomberg, SPSS and EViews bring theory into practice, and you can earn a Bloomberg Market Concepts certificate. Product development projects with researchers and business partners and an internship in semester eight complete the degree, and competency blocks let you add accounting and analytics, management, financial mathematics, languages, neuroscience or public governance. Graduates work as economists, consultants and data analysts in finance, government and business.
programmes.selectionNote: Score is maths or economics 40%, a second subject 40% and an oral motivation assessment 20%; each entry subject above 60%.

notes: KTU's own admission takes foreign citizens only into fee-paying places; an EU citizen can also apply through LAMA BPO for a state-funded place in an English programme (write to international@ktu.lt).
Yearly fee 2026/27 by field: €3,250 (business, economics, communication, linguistics), €4,201 (engineering, technology, informatics, sciences), €5,676 for the first 240 credits of Architecture.
Each entry subject needs an average above 60%, and programme pages allow at most three years since leaving school.
